newsitem.title: INDIA: China urges closer economic cooperation with India.
newsitem.headline: China urges closer economic cooperation with India.

text.p: Chinese President Jiang Zemin on Friday urged India and China to step up economic cooperation and explore new avenues in bilateral trade.

"I would like to call on both sides to make joint efforts to explore new ways and areas of economic cooperation so as to push our cooperation to a new high in the remaining years of the 20th century," Jiang told business leaders in New Delhi.
Jiang is the first Chinese President to visit India.
He said bilateral trade between the world's two most populous countries was poised to touch a new high in calendar 1996.
"It is expected to hit a record high this year as a total of nearly $1 billion had already been registered for the bilateral trade for the first eight months only," Jiang said.
According to official statistics, two-way trade totalled $1.16 billion in 1995, up from $895 million in 1994.
He asked businessmen in both nations to boost contacts and exchange information in areas like agriculture, energy, electrical machinery, environmental protection and high technology.
Earlier on Friday, India and China signed an agreement to extend most favoured nation status to each other's vessels in their respective ports.
Jiang said a number of favourable conditions existed for greater economic cooperation between India and China.

"First, the eased international situation and sustained, rapid growth of the economies of the Asia-Pacific region have provided a favourable external environment for enhancing economic cooperation," he said.
"Secondly, we both have given top priority to economic development."
Jiang said the geographical proximity of the two countries provided a good base for strengthening Sino-Indian economic ties.
"As the population of China and India amounts to 2.1 billion, the development of our two countries is vital to the well-being of one-third of the world's population," Jiang said.

Salman Haider, the highest ranking civil servant in India's Foreign Ministry, said at another news conference that a meeting of the joint economic group co-chaired by foreign ministers of the two countries would be held in the first quarter of 1997.
This group would work out a blueprint for expansion of trade beween the two countries, he said.
